Which system fits which task?

For a heavy launch vehicle leaving Earth, large thrust in a short time is essential. Chemical rockets, including proposed semi-cryogenic engines, suit this task. For a satellite adjusting its orbit over many days, low thrust with excellent propellant economy can be more useful, making electric propulsion attractive. When the main concern is the toxicity of the chemical carried by a spacecraft, the relevant subject is green propellant development.

These categories answer different questions: semi-cryogenic describes how cold the propellants must be stored; electric describes how the system supplies energy to accelerate the propellant; and green describes efforts to improve toxicity and environmental or handling characteristics. They are not 3 mutually exclusive boxes of the same classification. For example, a LOX-kerosene system is semi-cryogenic and may be considered cleaner than some alternatives, but it is still a chemical engine.

Recognise the Indian organisations correctly

  • LPSC: ISRO centre leading development of major liquid propulsion systems, including the semi-cryogenic SE2000 project and electric-propulsion work.
  • IPRC, Mahendragiri, Tamil Nadu: Site of semi-cryogenic powerhead tests, including the reported full-rating PHTA test on 5 September 2026.
  • Space Applications Centre (SAC), Ahmedabad, Gujarat: ISRO centre focused on instruments, communication and remote-sensing payloads and their applications. It is not the centre identified as the lead developer of SE2000.

The Gujarat connection is institutional: SAC in Ahmedabad contributes satellite payloads and applications, whereas the propulsion projects described here are led or tested by other ISRO facilities. Knowing the different roles prevents confusing a spacecraft's payload with the engine that moves it.

Keep development status separate from deployment

As of the 4 November 2026 content cutoff, the latest semi-cryogenic milestone established here is ISRO's 5 September 2026 PHTA test at the 200-tonne full-rating level; the SC120 replacement of L110 remains a development plan in that announcement. By contrast, GSAT-9 carried electric plasma thrusters on its 2017 mission. Indian green-propulsion payloads on POEM-4 were listed as technology demonstrations; proposed performance figures should not be treated as proof of widespread operational use.

Prelims focus

  • LOX + Isrosene: semi-cryogenic chemical propulsion; SE2000/SC120 is the Indian development example.
  • Electricity + xenon plasma: electric propulsion; GSAT-9 is an Indian flight example.
  • Less-toxic chemical alternatives: green propulsion; LPSC and POEM-4 are Indian development examples.
  • SAC is in Ahmedabad; IPRC is at Mahendragiri; LPSC leads propulsion development.
  • Trap: A successful subsystem test is not the same as a flown or fully qualified launch stage.
